# Appeal of Denial — Hip Arthroscopy (CPT 29914)

**Member:** Casey Hayes
**Member ID:** W225149976
**Payer/Plan:** Cigna (Commercial/ACA), Illinois
**Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-11
**Reference number:** POC-8E43F25837-44913
**Governing policy:** Cigna CMM-314 Hip Surgery - Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026 (https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-314%20Hip%20Surg%20Arthro%20%26%20Open%20Proc_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf), effective 2026-08-04

---

Dear Cigna Appeals Review Team,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), noticed on 2026-08-11. The stated reason was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I am asking Cigna to reconsider this decision, because the records already in my file address the plan's own indications for this surgery. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically needed, and I believe the information on file supports that.

## How my records match the plan's own criteria

The governing policy states:

> "femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

My records show the following, which speak to that standard:

- **Positive impingement finding / limited motion:** My exam findings document "positive provocative testing on the affected side" and "range of motion limited by pain." The policy also requires "positive anterior impingement sign" and "limited passive hip internal rotation." I am asking Cigna to review the exam documentation already submitted against these two specific elements, since my surgeon's notes describe painful, restricted motion and positive provocative testing on the affected hip.

- **Failed conservative management:** The policy states this indication requires:

  > "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration AND which must include the following (unless contraindicated):"

  My records document 24 months of progressive hip pain, NSAID use for 6 months with inadequate relief, a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-23 (partial relief lasting 3 weeks), and 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (18 visits, 2026-05-26 through 2026-07-21) with activity modification, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. Taken together, this is provider-directed non-surgical management spanning well over three months, without adequate relief.

- **Imaging findings:** My MRI arthrogram of the hip on 2026-06-08 documented an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement, an alpha angle of 68 degrees, preserved joint space, and Tonnis grade 0.

The policy separately states that certain radiographic findings make FAI surgery "not medically necessary":

> "Arthroscopic or open hip surgery for femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is considered not medically necessary for ANY other indication or condition, including ANY of the following radiographic findings:"

The specific excluded findings were not included in the materials available to me, so I am not able to confirm whether my imaging falls outside them. I would ask Cigna to identify, in its review, which if any of the listed excluded findings apply to my case, since my MRI report as documented (preserved joint space, Tonnis grade 0) does not on its face suggest advanced joint degeneration.

I also want to note that my requested procedure is for FAI/labral pathology, not synovectomy, and does not involve in-office diagnostic arthroscopy, capsular plication, or anterior inferior iliac spine/subspinous decompression. I understand those are addressed separately in the policy as either requiring different criteria or being classified as not medically necessary or experimental, and none of them describe what my surgeon has recommended.

## What I am asking

I am asking Cigna to reconsider the denial and to review the full documentation already submitted — the exam findings, the physical therapy discharge note, the medication and injection history, and the MRI report — against the plan's own FAI medical necessity criteria quoted above. If any specific piece of documentation is still considered missing, I would appreciate a clear, specific list of what is needed so that my surgeon's office and I can provide it promptly.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-07. I plan to submit it by logging into my.cigna.com to find the appropriate appeal form, or by calling 1-800-244-6224 or the number on my member ID card. I will also use the appeal mailing address printed on my denial letter.

Thank you for reconsidering my request.

Sincerely,

Casey Hayes
Member ID: W225149976

Date: [date of submission]
